eq:ch1.literal_latex_lines:
The $C$-coefficient functions are found to be
\bea
\delta C_{q\gets q'} (x,\mu_b) &=\delta_{q'q} \left[\delta(1-x)+{\cal O}(\alpha_s^2) \right]\; \label{eq:ch1},\\

eq:ch1perp.literal_latex_lines:
\bea
\delta C_{q\gets q'} (x,\mu_b) &=\delta_{q'q} \left[\delta(1-x)+{\cal O}(\alpha_s^2) \right]\; \label{eq:ch1},\\
\delta \hat C_{q'\gets q}^{\rm (SIDIS)}(z,\mu_b) &=\delta_{q'q} \left[\delta(1-z)+\frac{\alpha_s}{\pi}\left(\hat P_{q\gets q}^{c}(z) \ln z\right) \right]\; \label{eq:ch1perp},

eq:ch1_css.literal_latex_lines:
the relevant coefficient functions up to the first order in $\alpha_s$ (compare to Eq.~\eqref{eq:ch1perp} to determine relation to hard factor $H$) are given by~\cite{Koike:2006fn,Bacchetta:2013pqa,Yuan:2009dw,Echevarria:2014rua}:
\bea
\delta C_{q\gets q'}^{\rm (SIDIS)}(z,\mu_b)  (x,\mu_b) &=\delta_{q'q} \left[\delta(1-x)+\frac{\alpha_s}{\pi}\left(-2C_F\delta(1-x)\right) \right]\; \label{eq:ch1_css},\\

eq:ch1perp_css.literal_latex_lines:
\bea
\delta C_{q\gets q'}^{\rm (SIDIS)}(z,\mu_b)  (x,\mu_b) &=\delta_{q'q} \left[\delta(1-x)+\frac{\alpha_s}{\pi}\left(-2C_F\delta(1-x)\right) \right]\; \label{eq:ch1_css},\\
\delta \hat C_{q'\gets q}^{\rm (SIDIS)}(z,\mu_b) &=\delta_{q'q} \left[\delta(1-z)+\frac{\alpha_s}{\pi}\left(\hat P_{q\gets q}^{c}(z) \ln z -2C_F\delta(1-z)\right) \right]\; \label{eq:ch1perp_css},

policy: Literal reference text is preserved. Corrections/conversions are separate derived rows, never edits to the reference. A mismatch between papers is not automatically a production defect.
literal_kernel_discrepancy: The 2011 printed CA numerator contains z_h^2*(z^2+z1^2), whereas minus the 2009 AF density contains z_h*(z^2+z1^2) after aligning denominators. Preserve this discrepancy; overall signs, moments and operator conversions still require native derivation and review.
jet_application_caution: 1705.08443 treats semi-inclusive pp jets and has an independent jet-energy fraction; do not transplant its out-of-jet H into the small-qT ep formula. Prove the required reduction/overlap subtraction.
log_accuracy_caution: NLL-prime terminology is not uniform: KPSY uses it for approximate NLL with homogeneous evolution. Track retained perturbative coefficients explicitly.
